Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:10:1.hebrew: כותיה דר' יוחנן - דאמר: מטמאין דרבנן, לתלות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:10:1.english: In accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan - For he said [that] they deem [it] impure by Rabbinic law, to suspend [it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:10:2.hebrew: כמי שיש דעת לישאל - וקי"ל (נדה דף ד:), ברה"י ספיקו טמא; דבדבר שאין בו דעת לישאל, קי"ל (שם) דאפילו ברה"י ספיקו טהור:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:10:2.english: As that which has the capacity to be questioned - And it is established for us (Niddah 4b) [that] in a private domain, its uncertainty is [deemed] impure; for regarding a matter that does not have the capacity to be questioned, it is established for us (there) that even in a private domain, its uncertainty is [deemed] pure.

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:1:1.hebrew: לא שנו - דסמכינן אכרוכין אלא לקדשי הגבול — אם כהן הוא, אוכלים בקדשי הגבול. משהביא ראיה על אשה זו שהיא כשירה לכהונה, סומכין על הבנים הכרוכין אחריה לומר: בניה הן, ואינן חללין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:1:1.english: They taught - that we rely on [children] clinging [to her] only with regard to consecrated produce of the border: If he is a priest, they may eat consecrated produce of the border. Once he has brought proof regarding this woman that she is fit for the priesthood, we rely on the children who cling to her to say: They are her children, and they are not chalalim.

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:1:2.hebrew: אבל ליוחסין - אם יש בהן בנות, אינן נישאות לכהנים עד שיביאו ראיה שהן בנותיה של זו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:1:2.english: But with regard to lineage - If there are daughters among them, they may not marry priests until they bring proof that they are the daughters of this [woman].

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:1:3.hebrew: ור' יוחנן אמר אפילו ליוחסין - סמכינן אחזקה שהן כרוכין אחריה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:1:3.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Even with regard to lineage - We rely on the presumption that they are clinging to her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:2:1.hebrew: ואזדא רבי יוחנן לטעמיה - דאמר סמכינן אחזקה שהוחזקו ליכרך אצלה בחזקת שהיא אמו, אפילו לענין דיני נפשות — ליסקל ולישרף זה על זה, כדלקמן — וכ"ש ליוחסין, להכשר כהונה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:2:1.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his reasoning - For he said that we rely on presumptive status — where they were established to cling to her under the presumption that she is his mother — even regarding capital cases, to be stoned and to be burned on account of each other, as [explained] below; and all the more so regarding lineage, for fitness [to marry into the] priesthood.

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:2:2.hebrew: מלקין על החזקות - על דבר שאנו מחזיקים כן, ואפילו אין עדות בדבר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:2:2.english: One flogs on the basis of presumptions - On [the basis of] a matter that we presume [to be] so, and even if there is no testimony regarding the matter.

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:2:3.english: [The court] burns and stones, etc. - As [the Gemara] proceeds to explain them:

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:2:4.hebrew: ואין שורפין תרומה על החזקות - דבר שהוא טמא מתוך חזקה, ולא מתוך שהוא ראיה, ונגע בתרומה — כגון תינוק, שהוא סתמא מוחזק טמא, שמחפש באשפה שיש שם נבילות ושרצים, ונגע בתרומה — אין שורפין, אלא תולין. כדמפרש טעמא, כדאמרינן: העמד עיסה על חזקת טהרה, ואלו הוא ממיעוט תינוקות (הוא) שלא טיפח:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:2:4.english: But one does not burn teruma on the [basis of] presumptive status - An item that is ritually impure based on a presumption, and not based on direct observation, and it touched teruma — for example, a child, who is ordinarily presumed to be impure because he rummages in the rubbish dump where there are carcasses and creeping animals, and he touched teruma — we do not burn [the teruma], but rather suspend [its status], as [the Gemara later] explains the reason, as we say: Establish the dough upon its presumption of purity, and [consider that] this [child] is from the minority of children who did not handle [dough].

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:3:1.english: She had the presumptive status of a menstruating woman among her neighbors - That her neighbors saw that on that day she was wearing her garments of menstruation.

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:4:1.hebrew: איש ואשה תינוק ותינוקת שהגדילו בתוך הבית - בחזקת שהיא אשתו ואלו בניהם, ואין אנו מכירין בהם בעדות גמור:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:4:1.english: A man and a woman, a boy and a girl who grew up in the house - Under the presumption that she is his wife and these are their children, and we do not know them through conclusive testimony.

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:4:2.hebrew: נסקלין זה על זה - אם בא הבן על האשה, נסקל הבן עליה משום בא על אמו, והיא עליו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:4:2.english: They are stoned on account of each other - If the son has relations with the woman, the son is stoned on her account for having relations with his mother, and she [is stoned] on his account.

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:4:3.hebrew: ונשרפין זה על זה - אם בא האיש על הבת, דבתו בשריפה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:4:3.english: And they are burned due to each other - If the man engages in intercourse with the daughter, for [intercourse with] his daughter is [punished] by burning:

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:5:1.english: And a child riding on her shoulder, and she raised him - Under the presumption that he was her son:

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:6:1.english: And dough in his hand - It is certain that he took from the dough.

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:6:2.english: To handle - [That is, to dabble] in creeping animals and carcasses that are in the garbage dump.

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:7:1.hebrew: סמוך מיעוטא - דאין מטפחים לחזקה דעיסה, ואיתרע רובא דמטפחין. דלר' מאיר לא בטיל מעוטא לגמרי, דשמעינן ליה (נדה דף לב.) דחייש למיעוטא. הילכך, במקומו עומד, וכי משכח מידי לאיצטרופי בהדיה — מצטרף:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:7:1.english: Append the minority - [That is, append the minority] of [children] who do not handle [the dough] to the presumptive status of the dough, and the majority of [children] who handle [it] is weakened. For according to Rabbi Meir, a minority is not completely nullified, as we have heard him [say] (Niddah 32a) that he is concerned for a minority. Therefore, it stands in its place, and when it finds something to join with it, it joins.

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:7:2.hebrew: מיעוטא כמאן דליתיה דמי - דבטיל ליה לגבי רובא, ורבנן לטעמייהו דלא חיישי למיעוט (שם):
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:7:2.english: The minority is considered like it does not exist - For it is nullified relative to the majority, and the Rabbis [follow] their reasoning, that they do not take a minority into account (ibid.).

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:8:1.hebrew: זו היא ששורפין עליה את התרומה - חזקה ששורפין עליה את התרומה — חזקת תינוקות שמחזיקין לטפח, שורפין עליה תרומה; דהאי מטמאין דקאמרי רבנן, לשרוף קאמרי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:8:1.english: This is that based on which one burns the teruma - [The] presumption based on which one burns the teruma [is] the presumption of children, who are presumed to handle [dough] — one burns teruma based on it; for this [ruling of] "they deem it impure" that the Rabbis stated, they stated [it meaning] to burn [it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:8:2.hebrew: ור' יוחנן אמר אפילו ליוחסין - סמכינן אחזקה, שהן כרוכין אחריה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:8:2.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Even for [matters of] lineage - We rely on the presumption that they (the children) cling after her (their mother):

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:8:3.hebrew: שורפים וסוקלין כו' - כדמפרש להו ואזיל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:8:3.english: They burn and they stone, etc. - As [the Gemara] explains them as it proceeds.

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:8:4.hebrew: אין זו חזקה ששורפין כו' - וכי אמרי רבנן, שהספק טמא לתלות קאמרי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:8:4.english: This is not a presumption that one burns [teruma] based on it, etc. - And when the Rabbis say [that the dough is impure], they mean only that it is to be left in suspense — [the teruma is neither eaten nor burned, but set aside until its status is clarified]:

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:9:1.hebrew: שרצים - צב הדומה לצפרדע; הצב טמא, והצפרדע טהור:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:9:1.english: Creeping animals - [Such as] a tzav [lizard], which resembles a frog; the tzav is impure, and the frog is pure.

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:9:2.hebrew: מטפלים שם - עושים נפולין נפולין, חתיכות חתיכות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:9:2.english: Attending to their work there - They produce chips and scraps, pieces upon pieces:

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:9:3.english: And pieces were found in the dough - And it is not known whether [they are] of creeping animals or of frogs.

Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:9:4.hebrew: אם רוב שרצים - אם הבית מוחזקת להיות שרצים מצוים שם יותר מצפרדעים — טמא, אף לישרף, דחזקה ורובא דאיתיה קמן הוא. אבל ההיא דתינוק — רובא דליתיה קמן הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 80a:9:4.english: If the majority are creeping animals - If the house is presumed to have creeping animals found there more than frogs, [the dough is] impure, even to [the point of being] burned, for it is [both] a presumption and a majority that is present before us. But that [case] of the child is a majority that is not present before us.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 80a:1:1.hebrew: לא שנו אלא בקדשי הגבול - לפי' רש"י, הא דאמרינן דמהני כרוכין, היינו דוקא לתרומה — שאם הוא כהן והביא ראיה על האשה, אין צריך להביא ראיה על הבנים להאכילן בתרומה. וקשה: דמשמע דמכל מקום צריך שיהו כרוכין להאכילן בתרומה, ובפרק האשה שנתארמלה (כתובות דף כה:) אמרינן: ״האומר בני זה וכהן הוא — נאמן להאכילו בתרומה, ואינו נאמן להשיאו אשה״, אלמא לא בעינן שיהו כרוכין אחריה! ויש לומר: דרב תנא הוא ופליג. ורבינו תם פירש: דרב סבר כמאן דאמר (שם כד:) ״אין מעלין מתרומה ליוחסין״, ולכך נאמן להאכילו תרומה כיון דבידו הוא; ומתני' דהכא סברה כמאן דאמר (שם) ״מעלין מתרומה ליוחסין״. והכא הכי פירושו: ״לא שנו אלא בקדשי הגבול״ — פירוש: בכל דבר קדושה, כגון לתרומה, ולנשיאת כפים, ולהשיאו אשה; ״אבל ליוחסין — לא״, כלומר: לסקול על ידו, דקאמר ״זה הבן וזו אמו״, והבן בא עליה — לא מהימן. והיינו דקאמר: ״ואזדא רבי יוחנן לטעמיה, דאמר סוקלין ושורפים על החזקות״. ולפירוש הקונטרס, ״אבל ליוחסין״ — כגון להיות משמש בנו על גבי המזבח לא מהימן — צריך לומר דהכי מייתי ראיה: סוקלין ושורפין על החזקות, וכל שכן דנאמן ליוחסין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 80a:1:1.english: "They taught [this] only with regard to consecrated items of the border" - According to Rashi’s explanation, that which we say that [children] clinging [to their mother] is effective, this applies specifically to teruma — that if he is a priest and brought proof regarding the woman, he does not need to bring proof regarding the children in order to feed them teruma. And this is difficult, for it implies that in any case they must be clinging [to her] in order to feed them teruma; yet in the chapter [entitled] "The Woman Who Was Widowed" (Ketubot 25b), we say: "One who says, 'This is my son and he is a priest,' is believed to feed him teruma, but is not believed to marry him to a woman [of priestly stock]." Evidently, we do not require that they be clinging to her! And one can say: Rav is a Tanna and disagrees. And Rabbeinu Tam explained: Rav holds in accordance with the one who says (ibid. 24b) that one does not elevate from teruma to lineage, and therefore [the father] is believed to feed him teruma since it is within his power; whereas the Mishnah here holds in accordance with the one who says that one does elevate from teruma to lineage. And here, this is its explanation: "They taught [this] only with regard to consecrated items of the border" — meaning, regarding any matter of sanctity, such as for teruma, for the raising of hands [for the priestly blessing], and to marry him to a woman; "but with regard to lineage — no," that is to say, to stone [someone] on his account, such that if [witnesses or the father] said: "This is the son and this is his mother," and the son had intercourse with her, he is not believed. And that is why [the Gemara] says: "And Rabbi Yoḥanan follows his line of reasoning, as he said: The court stones and burns on the basis of presumptions." And according to the explanation of the Kunteres [Rashi], [where Reish Lakish said] "but with regard to lineage" — such as that his son is not believed to serve upon the Altar — one must say that this is how [the Gemara] brings proof: The court stones and burns on the basis of presumptions, and all the more so that he is believed with regard to lineage.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 80a:6:1.hebrew: שדרכו של תינוק לטפח - פירש בקונטרס: לטפח באשפה. וא"ת: כיון שהתינוק אינו ודאי טמא, אם כן, אמאי נקט "תינוק שנמצא בצד העיסה"? לינקוט "שנגע בעיסה"! ועוד קשה: דאמרינן בתוספתא (דטהרות פ"ג ע"ש): "מפני מה אמרו שהתינוק טמא? משום דנשים נדות מגפפות ומנשקות אותו", והכא מפרש משום דמטפחין באשפה?! לכך פירש ר"ת: שהתינוק ודאי טמא — כדמפרש בתוספתא; ולכך נקט שנמצא בצד העיסה ובצק בידו — דהשתא ספק הוא: אם נטלה מן העיסה וטימא את העיסה, או שמא אדם טהור נכנס לשם ונטל את העיסה ונתן לתינוק. ובהא פליגי ר' מאיר ורבנן: דר' מאיר מטהר — דתלינן באדם טהור; וחכמים מטמאין — מפני שדרכו של תינוק לטפח (פי' בעיסה), ויש לנו לומר שנטלה. ובכי האי גוונא פליגי בתוספתא גבי תינוק שנמצא בצד הקבר ושושנים בידו, ואינו יודע אם התינוק נטלן או אדם טהור נתנן לו: ר' מאיר מטהר, וחכמים מטמאין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 80a:6:1.english: "Because it is the manner of a child to handle" - The Kunteres [Rashi] explained: To handle [items] in the rubbish. And should you say: Since the child is not definitely impure, if so, why did [the mishna] formulate [the case as] "a child who was found alongside the dough"? Let it formulate [the case as one] where he touched the dough! Furthermore, it is difficult, for we say in the Tosefta (Tahorot ch. 3, see there): "For what reason did they say that a child is impure? Because menstruant women embrace and kiss him." Yet here [Rashi] explains [the reason is] because they handle [items] in the rubbish?! Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam explained that the child is definitely impure, as is explained in the Tosefta. And therefore [the mishna] formulated [the case as one] where he was found alongside the dough and dough was in his hand, for now it is an uncertainty: whether he took it from the dough and [thereby] rendered the dough impure, or perhaps a ritually pure person entered there, took the [piece of] dough, and gave it to the child. And about this Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis disagree: for Rabbi Meir deems [the dough] pure, as we attribute [the giving of the dough] to a pure person; and the Rabbis deem [it] impure, "because it is the manner of a child to handle [items]" — meaning, in the dough — and we must say that he [himself] took it. And in a similar manner, they disagree in the Tosefta regarding a child who was found alongside a grave with lilies in his hand, and one does not know whether the child took them or a ritually pure person gave them to him: Rabbi Meir deems [it] pure, and the Rabbis deem [it] impure.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 80a:7:1.hebrew: סמוך מיעוטא לחזקה ואיתרע ליה רובא - פירוש: והוי רוב כמאן דליתיה. וקשה, דבריש פרק בתרא דיבמות (דף קיט.) אמרינן גבי האשה שהלך בעלה למדינת הים וצרתה עמו ושמעה האשה שמת בעלה: ר' מאיר אומר, "לא תנשא ולא מתיבמת", לפי דרוב נשים מתעברות ויולדות, ואיכא למימר שהצרה שהלכה עמו ילדה, והויא האשה שנשארה פטורה מן היבום; ומיעוט מפילות ילדיהן. וקאמר ר"מ דאמרינן סמוך מיעוטא לחזקה — שהרי היתה בחזקת זקוקה ליבום כשהלך בעלה למדינת הים ולא היה לו בנים — והוה ליה פלגא ופלגא; כלומר, דמיעוטא וחזקה חשובין כנגד אותן רוב דנשים מתעברות ויולדות, והוה פלגא ופלגא, ולא תנשא ולא תתייבם. וכמו כן אית לן למימר הכא! וכי תימא: דאין הכי נמי, והא דמטהר רבי מאיר היינו משום דתינוק אין בו דעת לישאל, וכל ספק שאין בו דעת לישאל, אף ברשות היחיד, ספיקו טהור — דהא בהדיא אמרינן בסמוך בשמעתין דעשאוהו חכמים כמי שיש בו דעת לישאל! וי"ל: שאין זה רוב חשוב, אלא רוב גרוע; לכך מרעי ליה מיעוטא וחזקה. ותדע שאין חשוב — מדאמרינן בסמוך: "עשאוהו חכמים כמי שיש בו דעת לישאל", ולכך מטמאין את העיסה; ואי הוה רוב חשוב, אפילו אין בו דעת לישאל הוה לן לטמויי! וע"כ צריך לומר כן, דאם לא כן, קשה אליבא דרבנן: דהא רבנן קאמרי התם גבי הלך בעלה למדינת הים ושמעה שמת: "תנשא", דקסברי דמיעוט כמאן דליתיה דמי, ורובא וחזקה — רובא עדיף; ואם כן, אמאי קאמר הכא רבי יוחנן אליבא דרבנן: "אין זו חזקה ששורפין עליה תרומה"? אלא שמע מינה שאין זה רוב חשוב, ולפיכך התם דרוב חשוב — תנשא. (ולפי זה ניחא מה שמקשים העולם, דקשה להו גבי: "שני דברים אין בו דעת לישאל ועשאוהו כמי שיש בו דעת לישאל", וקא חשיב דתינוק, ומקשין: מאי איריא שיש בו דעת לישאל? תיפוק ליה משום דסבירא להו לרבנן במיעוטא כמאן דליתיה, ורובא וחזקה — רובא עדיף, וא"כ אפילו אין בו דעת לישאל טמא, דהא אין זה ספק טומאה אלא ודאי טומאה! ש"מ שאין זה רוב חשוב, ואי לאו דעשאוהו חכמים כמי שיש בו דעת לישאל, לא היו מטמאים):
Tosafot on Kiddushin 80a:7:1.english: Append the minority to the presumptive status, and the majority is weakened - Explanation: And the majority is considered like it does not exist [for Rabbi Meir deems the dough completely pure]. And it is difficult: For at the beginning of the last chapter of Yevamot (119a), we say regarding the woman whose husband went overseas and her co-wife was with him, and the woman heard that her husband died: Rabbi Meir says, "She may neither marry nor enter levirate marriage," because a majority of women conceive and give birth, and one can say that the co-wife who went with him gave birth, so the woman who remained would be exempt from levirate marriage, whereas a minority miscarry their fetuses. And Rabbi Meir states that we say: Append the minority to the presumptive status — for she had the presumptive status of being bound to levirate marriage when her husband went overseas and he had no children — and it becomes fifty-fifty; that is to say, that the minority and presumptive status are considered equal against that majority of women who conceive and give birth, and it is fifty-fifty, so she may neither marry nor enter levirate marriage. And likewise we ought to say here [that it should be a fifty-fifty doubt]! And if you say: Indeed that is so, and that which Rabbi Meir deems pure is because a child lacks the capacity to be questioned, and any uncertainty regarding [an entity that] lacks the capacity to be questioned, even in a private domain, its uncertainty is pure — [that cannot be,] for we explicitly say nearby in our sugya that the Sages treated him like one who has the capacity to be questioned! And one can say: This is not a significant majority, but rather a weak majority; therefore, the minority and the presumptive status weaken it [completely]. And you may know that it is not significant — from that which we say nearby: "The Sages treated him like one who has the capacity to be questioned," and for that reason they deem the dough impure; for if it were a significant majority, even [if] he lacks the capacity to be questioned, we should have deemed it impure! And perforce one must say so, for if not so, it is difficult according to the Rabbis: For the Rabbis say there, regarding [a woman whose] husband went overseas and she heard that he died, "she may marry," as they hold that the minority is considered like it does not exist, and [between] a majority and a presumptive status, the majority takes precedence; and if so, why does Rabbi Yoḥanan say here according to the Rabbis: "This is not a presumption that one burns teruma based on it"? Rather, learn from this that this is not a significant majority, and therefore there, where it is a significant majority, she may marry. (And according to this, that which people ask is resolved, for they find it difficult regarding [the baraita]: "Two things do not have the capacity to be questioned, and they treated them like one who has the capacity to be questioned," and it counts a child, and they ask: Why specifically [because] he has the capacity to be questioned? Let it be derived because the Rabbis hold that a minority is considered like it does not exist, and [between] a majority and a presumptive status, the majority takes precedence, and if so, even [if] he lacks the capacity to be questioned, [the dough should be] impure, for this is not a doubtful impurity, but a definite impurity! Learn from this that this is not a significant majority, and were it not that the Sages treated him like one who has the capacity to be questioned, they would not have deemed [it] impure.):
